_about: Body-movement input tuning (Feature Brief 05). Edit and refresh the page - no rebuild needed. Keys starting with _ are comments. Any key omitted falls back to the default in src/input/bodyTuning.ts.
_upperBody: Lean and jump are measured from the two SHOULDER landmarks only. Nothing here reads the hips - a desk-height webcam frames you from the chest up, so the hips are outside the frame and MediaPipe only guesses at them.
_leanUnits: The lean value is the SINE of your shoulder-line tilt: 0.09 = 5deg, 0.16 = 9deg, 0.26 = 15deg, 0.34 = 20deg.
_jumpUnits: Jump values are fractions of your own shoulder width (~40cm on an adult), so 0.12 is a rise of about 5cm. Being fractions of your own size, they mean the same thing at any distance from the camera.
_tuning: Run cv_model/Nishit_Frontend/diagnose_body.py to see what YOUR body actually produces, then set leanEnter to roughly half your comfortable peak. Do not guess these.
_leanEnter: Shoulder tilt needed to START a lean. Must be above leanExit. Lower = more sensitive.
_leanExit: Tilt below which the lean ENDS. The gap is what stops boundary oscillation.
_leanScale: Pure sensitivity multiplier. Raise above 1 if leaning feels like hard work.
_leanRecentreRate: How fast the neutral point follows your resting posture, per second. Fixes 'one side works, the other does not', which is caused by drifting off-square after calibrating. Lower it if a slow deliberate lean gets absorbed; raise it if the asymmetry comes back.
_jumpHeightFraction: Shoulder rise as a fraction of shoulder width. Lower it if small hops are missed.
_jumpMinVelocity: How fast you must be rising. This is what separates a jump from standing up.
_jumpVelocityWindowMs: How far back the jump height/velocity checks look.
_jumpRequireLabel: Leave false. True also demands the pipeline's own 'jumping' label, which is computed from the hips and never fires in a chest-up framing. Only useful with a full-body camera.
_jumpBaselineRate: How fast the standing shoulder height a jump is measured against follows you, per second. Frozen while you are off the ground. Without it, settling into a chair leaves a permanent fake 'rise'.
